categories.name: STM32 Board Bring-up & Startup
categories.description: Covers the target board and MCU constraints, board-supported UART mapping, reset initialization, and reliable startup after flashing.
requirements: The firmware shall target the NUCLEO-C5A3ZG board, reference MB2310.
The firmware shall execute on an STM32C5A3ZGT6 MCU with a Cortex-M33 processor, single-precision FPU and DSP capability.
The firmware shall operate within a maximum device resource envelope of 144 MHz CPU clock, 1 MiB Flash and 256 KiB SRAM.
The application shall not require an external sensor, external memory, network connection, RTOS or NPU.
The application shall use the UART instance and pins supported by the selected board configuration and shall not assume unsupported pin mappings.
On reset, the application shall initialize the MCU clock, FPU and serial console.
The application shall start correctly after flashing and a hardware reset.
The firmware shall be flashable to the physical board and shall start after reset.
The application shall complete clock and FPU initialization before starting ML runtime initialization or executing FP32 inference.
The application shall initialize the test status, vector counters and comparison results to a known state after every reset before beginning the test sequence.

categories.name: UART Console & Result Reporting
categories.description: Covers ST-LINK VCP configuration, transmission checks, startup and per-vector output, result formatting, and final status reporting.
requirements: The application shall report five known-vector comparisons through the ST-LINK Virtual COM Port.
After reset, the application shall produce a concise and deterministic PASS/FAIL result.
The application shall use the on-board STLINK-V3EC Virtual COM Port at 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit and no flow control.
The application shall print one deterministic result line per vector and a final summary.
If any vector or runtime operation fails, the final status shall be FAIL and the failing condition shall be reported while console output remains available.
The application shall multiply console display values by 1000 and print them as integers.
The application shall print the model SHA-256 identifier at startup.
The application shall print ML_RUNTIME_READY only after successful model and runtime initialization.
The application shall print exactly one ML_VECTOR result line for each executed vector.
The application shall detect an unsuccessful console transmission for each required startup, vector-result and final-status message.
Each ML_VECTOR result line shall identify the reference vector and indicate the outcome of its FP32 comparison.
The serial console shall report all five test vectors.
The application shall print ML_SUMMARY passed=5 total=5 status=PASS only when all five reference-vector comparisons and cleanup succeed; otherwise it shall not report a PASS summary.

categories.name: Build, Memory & Release Configuration
categories.description: Covers compatible firmware and runtime builds, linker and SRAM/Flash constraints, reproducibility, and delivery of project and validation artifacts.
requirements: The application shall not require dynamic heap allocation for the test sequence.
All generated model sources, runtime libraries and application objects shall use a mutually compatible Cortex-M33 CPU/FPU ABI.
The final firmware shall link without unresolved model or runtime symbols, ABI mismatch errors or overlapping memory regions.
The generated linker memory placement shall fit within the target MCU Flash and SRAM limits.
The complete firmware shall build and link successfully for NUCLEO-C5A3ZG.
A fresh rebuild of the same source and model shall produce the same functional behavior on the target board.
The project shall deliver STM32 project source code.
The project shall deliver the final firmware binary/ELF artifact.
The project shall deliver the model SHA-256 identifier.
The project shall deliver a captured serial log showing startup, five vector results and the final PASS/FAIL summary.
The project shall deliver a short validation record stating the board used, firmware build result, flash result and observed inference result.
The complete startup and five-vector test sequence shall execute without runtime stack overflow and with all stack, static, activation, context and I/O storage within the target SRAM allocation.

categories.name: ONNX Model & ST AI Runtime
categories.description: Covers preservation and conversion of the ONNX model, embedded model storage, ST AI runtime integration, and model initialization and cleanup.
requirements: The STM32 application shall execute the supplied FP32 ONNX model on the MCU CPU.
The application shall use c5_dense_relu.onnx unchanged.
The deployed model shall be an FP32 ONNX model using opset 17 and IR 8, with one input tensor named input and one output tensor named output, both having shape [1,2].
The model graph shall consist of MatMul, Add and ReLU operations.
The application shall perform no preprocessing or postprocessing other than direct FP32 input and output handling.
The deployed firmware shall execute the compiled neural-network model using the ST AI runtime.
The application shall not use a handwritten replacement of the model equations as valid model inference.
The application shall initialize the generated ML network and all required activation, context and I/O buffers.
The application shall deinitialize the ML runtime after the test sequence completes.
The model shall be compiled for STM32C5 CPU execution using an ST AI compatible C runtime.
The supplied ONNX model shall be converted into deployable STM32C5 inference code without changing the model graph or weights.
The project shall deliver compiled ML model sources and required runtime integration files.
The firmware shall embed the model weights and biases in the firmware image, and inference shall not depend on external model or weight storage.
The SHA-256 identifier printed at startup shall correspond to the model actually embedded and used by the deployed firmware.

categories.name: Inference Test Harness & Verification
categories.description: Covers the fixed reference-vector sequence, inference execution, FP32 comparisons and tolerances, and handling of test or runtime failures.
requirements: The application shall execute each of the five reference input vectors exactly once.
For every reference vector, the application shall compare both FP32 outputs with the expected values before formatting them for display.
Any initialization failure, inference failure, non-finite output, deinitialization failure or console transmission failure shall cause the test to fail.
The application shall execute the positive reference vector with input [1,2] and expected output [0.5,4], displaying [500,4000] in milli-units.
The application shall execute the first_clamped reference vector with input [-2,1] and expected output [0,4], displaying [0,4000] in milli-units.
The application shall execute the second_clamped reference vector with input [3,-1] and expected output [7.5,0], displaying [7500,0] in milli-units.
The application shall execute the zero_input reference vector with input [0,0] and expected output [0.5,0], displaying [500,0] in milli-units.
The application shall execute the both_clamped reference vector with input [-1,-1] and expected output [0,0], displaying [0,0] in milli-units.
The application shall compare each original FP32 output using an absolute tolerance of 0.000001 and a relative tolerance of 0.
Each vector shall match the expected FP32 result within the defined tolerance.
Wrong, missing or non-finite outputs, or any ML runtime failure, shall not be counted as a pass.
The application shall execute the five reference vectors in a fixed, documented order on every test run.
